headline: Six of seven majors above their 200-day lines but momentum is stalling; whale behavior and fund flows diverge as leverage sits expensive and crowded.
paragraphs: The trend frame is intact. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all trade above their 200-day simple moving averages, and so does ADA, with only Dogecoin below. That is a broad institutional bid. Yet the momentum picture is fractured. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 67.7 with MACD still above its signal line, which is the posture of a trend that has moved but is not accelerating. Ethereum RSI is 67.3 but MACD has crossed below its signal, a divergence: price is elevated, momentum is turning. Solana RSI is 67.1 with MACD still above signal, but its realized volatility is 59.8 percent, the highest bar for any of these assets except Ethereum at 67.8 percent. XRP's RSI is only 62, well below the overbought threshold, even though it trades above its 200-day line. Dogecoin is the clearest break: it sits below the 200-day line with RSI at 54.7, MACD below signal, and is down 10 percent on the week. Six in one regime, one in another. Over the month the story shifts: Bitcoin up 19.5 percent, Ethereum up 28.9 percent, Solana up 31.4 percent, XRP up 23.9 percent. On the day and week, though, every major asset is down or sideways. Bitcoin down 0.8 percent on the day, up only 1.1 percent on the week. Ethereum down 0.6 percent on the day, up 1.2 percent on the week. Solana down 0.8 percent on the day, up 8.8 percent on the week. This is a market resting after a run, not rolling over, but the wheels are losing momentum.

Leverage is both expensive and tilted toward length. Bitcoin funding on OKX is 0.71 basis points per eight hours, which annualizes to 7.8 percent. Ethereum is 1.0 basis points, or 11 percent annualized. Those are not extreme, but they are not cheap: traders holding long positions are paying to stay in. The long-to-short ratio on Bitcoin is 1.29, meaning 29 percent more notional value is long than short. For Ethereum it is 1.46, a more pronounced lean. Solana swings the other way: 1.91 ratio and negative funding at minus 0.55 basis points (minus 6.0 percent annualized), which means longs are being paid to hold. That inversion is worth flagging: when most majors are positively funded but one is negatively funded, traders disagree on direction in that one asset. Over the last hour on Ethereum, shorts have been liquidated at a 6.3-to-1 ratio; on Solana, shorts have still been liquidated more than longs, but on XRP, longs have been liquidated at a 21-to-1 ratio even as the asset climbs on the month. The crowd is betting long, positions are large, and the moves that liquidate them are sharp.

Whale behavior and institutional inflows paint different pictures. Over the last twenty-four hours, Bitcoin has moved $178.6 million off exchanges, a genuine outflow from trading venues to self-custody. That is the posture of confidence, or at least conviction. Yet look at the weekly pattern: the week ending August 25 saw $1.09 billion move onto exchanges, the three prior weeks averaged $418 million onto exchanges each. The current week, ending September 1, shows $211 million moved onto exchanges. The direction has flipped. Bitcoin ETF flows, by contrast, show sustained institutional buying: $216.7 million inflow on August 31 alone, $803.6 million net inflow over the last five sessions, and ten consecutive days of inflows for Ethereum ETF, $787.7 million over the last five sessions. So the traditional-finance bid is consistent, but the whale move off exchanges over the last day contradicts the week ending August 25, when whales were sellers. The stablecoin float is $308.9 billion, up 1.1 percent over the month, a mild accumulation of dry powder. That is not panic selling and not exuberant buying power deployment either.

Fear and Greed sits at 69, labeled Greed, and it has ranged from 25 to 74 over the last thirty days. The gauge has spent time in deep fear and now sits firmly in greed, but the tape contradicts the label. Market capitalization fell 4.48 percent on the day while prices fell between 0.1 and 0.8 percent, a steeper drawdown in total value than in individual assets, a sign of altcoin weakness outpacing the majors. Bitcoin dominance is 59.1 percent, high by modern standards. The day's movers show scattered interest: Curve, Filecoin, and Arbitrum each up more than nine percent, while smaller names like CC, VVV, and a Trump-themed token are down six to eight percent. That dispersion is what greed without conviction looks like.

Two windows tell the real story. Every major asset is down on the day and mixed on the week, but all are up on the month by double digits. That is not a rally; that is recovery from a drawdown that sits unfinished. Bitcoin is 37.5 percent below its twelve-month high of $124,739, Ethereum 47.9 percent below $4,707, Solana 58.8 percent below $247.60. The distance from the all-time high is still the dominant feature. Difficulty on the Bitcoin network has crept up 1.4 percent as the retarget window approaches block 585, a sign of steady hash power addition even as spot prices languish.

Watch for three shifts: the first is a move back onto exchanges after today's outflow, which would signal whales reconsidering the hold thesis; the second is a break below the 200-day line in Bitcoin or Ethereum, which would collapse the regime frame; the third is a flip in ETF flows from inflow to outflow, which would show the traditional-finance bid has exhausted. None of those is imminent in this tape. What stands out is the rest: high leverage, high greed gauge, month-long gains, day-long losses, and fund flows that outpace whale moves in conviction but not in size. That is the mark of a market taking a breather between two ideas about direction, and the tape is not yet ready to choose.
